best_for: Windows users with a capable graphics card who want to run image and video AI models on their own PC without setting up Python, PyTorch and CUDA by hand.
description:
Comfy Desktop is the official desktop app for ComfyUI, the node-based engine for generative AI, made by Comfy Org. It downloads and sets up everything ComfyUI needs, including its own Python with PyTorch and GPU libraries, so it is the only thing you install.

You can keep several ComfyUI builds side by side, each with its own version, models and custom nodes, update them in place, and take a snapshot to roll back when an update or a custom node breaks something. Existing portable or git installs can be brought in. Inside ComfyUI you connect nodes into workflows that run open models such as Flux and Wan, or open a ready-made app and just supply the input.

points.title: Free to run on your own PC
points.text: Local builds cost nothing and have no feature tiers or trial. Comfy Org says ComfyUI is open source under GPL-3.0; the Comfy Desktop app's own repository offers its code under AGPL 3.0 or a commercial license. After setup, local builds can run without an internet connection.

points.title: Comfy Cloud is optional and paid
points.text: The app can also open Comfy Cloud, which runs workflows on Comfy Org's GPUs. That needs a Comfy account and spends Comfy Credits while the GPU runs.

points.title: Hardware and disk space
points.text: Comfy Desktop needs Windows 10 or later. A dedicated NVIDIA or AMD graphics card is recommended but not required, and each build needs at least 4.85 GB of free space before you add any models, which are the large part.

points.title: Windows x64 here, installed per user
points.text: This listing has the x64 installer, which installs for the current user only. Comfy Org also offers a Windows Arm64 installer, where local builds need an NVIDIA graphics card.

points.title: Mac and Linux builds exist, but not here
points.text: Comfy Org also makes Comfy Desktop for Apple silicon Macs on macOS 13 or later and for x64 Linux as an AppImage or .deb. This listing covers Windows only.

points.title: Long version history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 144 versions, so you can go back to an earlier release of the app if a new one gives you trouble. The app also updates itself.
